records.title: Astra 1.8L Z18XER Water Pump / Timing Chain Wear
records.description: 2008-2009 Saturn Astra is the Belgian-built Opel Astra H rebadged. The 1.8L Z18XER engine's water pump is driven from the timing chain — pump failure can jam the chain and bend valves. Common at 80,000-130,000 miles. Parts have become scarce in North America since Saturn / Opel withdrew.
records.solution: Replace water pump WITH timing chain kit as preventive service ($1,200-$2,000 at independent specialist). Parts may need to be sourced through Opel/Vauxhall channels (UK, Germany). Catastrophic pump seize means head rebuild ($3,500+). Do not delay if there is any whining or coolant weep from the front of the engine.

records.title: 2.4L Ecotec Excessive Oil Consumption
records.description: Auras with the 2.4L Ecotec four-cylinder (XE) can develop high oil consumption as they age, often attributed to worn piston oil-control rings allowing oil past the rings into the combustion chamber. Owners report burning roughly a quart every 1,000-2,000 miles, which can lead to low-oil conditions and engine wear if not monitored. This is a known weakness across the GM 2.4L Ecotec family.
records.solution: Monitor oil level frequently between changes and top off as needed; severe cases require piston/ring replacement or a short-block. Keeping to high-quality oil and regular change intervals helps. Some owners catch it early via the oil-life monitor and frequent checks.

citations.title: GM 2.4L Ecotec Engine Specs, Problems, Reliability (MotorReviewer)
Common 2.4 Ecotec Engine Problems (Rx Mechanic)

records.title: 3.6L Random/Multiple-Cylinder Misfire
records.description: The 3.6L V6 Auras are reported to throw misfire codes, frequently as a downstream symptom of the stretched timing chains but also from worn ignition coils/spark plugs or carbon buildup on the direct-injection intake valves. Owners experience rough idle, hesitation, and a check engine light. P0300 with cylinder-specific misfire codes is common.
records.solution: Diagnose root cause: inspect/measure timing chain deviation first (since chains are a known weak point), then replace spark plugs and any failed ignition coils. Walnut-blast carbon from intake valves if buildup is present. Address timing chains if correlation codes accompany the misfire.

citations.title: P0300 on 2007-2009 Saturn Aura: Random Misfire Causes and Fixes

records.title: 3.6L V6 (LY7) Stretched Timing Chains
records.description: The early GM 3.6L high-feature V6 (used in Aura XR) is prone to premature timing chain stretch, sometimes appearing as early as 50,000-100,000 miles. As the chains wear, camshaft-to-crankshaft timing drifts out of spec, setting correlation codes and eventually causing rough running, reduced power, and potential engine damage if ignored. A cold-start rattle is a common early warning sign.
records.solution: Replace all three timing chains, tensioners, and guides (a major job). GM issued Special Coverage Adjustment #11340 (extending warranty to 10 years/120,000 miles on affected engines and requiring ECM reprogramming in some cases). Use the correct oil and change intervals to slow wear.
symptoms: Check engine light with timing correlation codes

citations.title: P0019 on 2007-2009 Saturn Aura 3.6L: Stretched Timing Chain Causes and Fixes

P0017 Saturn Code Meaning, Causes, Symptoms & Tech Notes

records.title: Aura 3.6L LY7 V6 Timing Chain Stretch
records.description: The GM 3.6L LY7/LLT "High Feature" V6 in 2007-2009 Saturn Aura XR (and shared Chevy Malibu / Pontiac G6 / Cadillac CTS) develops timing chain stretch typically by 80,000-150,000 miles. Same root cause family as the LLT in Enclave/LaCrosse/Acadia — extended oil intervals starve the chain.
records.solution: Full timing chain kit ($1,800-$3,000 at independent) including primary and secondary chains, all tensioners and guides. Switch to 5,000-7,500 mile dexos1 oil intervals. Catastrophic chain skip means cylinder head damage ($4,000+).

records.title: Body Control Module Connection Corrosion (Brake Lights / Cruise)
records.description: Increased resistance can develop in the Body Control Module (BCM) electrical connection on 2008 Auras, causing voltage fluctuations. This can affect exterior lighting (including brake lights), electronic stability control, vehicle speed control (cruise), and related systems, creating intermittent electrical faults. It was significant enough to prompt a safety recall.
records.solution: Covered by NHTSA recall 14V252000 — dealers secured the wiring harness to the BCM with a spacer and applied dielectric lubricant to the connectors. Out of warranty, cleaning/repairing the BCM connector and applying dielectric grease addresses the high-resistance connection.
symptoms: Stability control / traction control warning lights

citations.title: 2008 Saturn Aura Recalls (Cars.com) — campaign 14V252000 BCM
98 Complaints: 2007 Saturn Aura Electrical System Problems

records.title: EVAP Canister Purge Valve Failure (Check Engine Light)
records.description: Auras commonly throw EVAP emissions faults, most often from a stuck-open or failing canister purge solenoid/valve (and sometimes a clogged charcoal canister or faulty fuel-tank pressure sensor). The result is a persistent check engine light and potential emissions-test failure. The gas cap is worth checking first but is usually not the cause of the P0496 flow-during-non-purge code.
records.solution: Confirm the gas cap is tight, inspect EVAP vacuum lines for cracks, then replace the canister purge solenoid/valve if it is stuck open. Replace the charcoal canister or fuel-tank pressure sensor if those are at fault.

records.title: Premature Warped Front Brake Rotors
records.description: First-generation Auras (especially 2007) are widely reported to warp their front brake rotors prematurely, producing steering-wheel and front-end shimmy under braking. Owners report rotors warping within a few thousand miles and needing repeated resurfacing or replacement, in some cases every 10,000 miles. The issue was acknowledged by service staff as a design weakness on 2007 and, to a lesser degree, 2008 cars.
records.solution: Replace the rotors and pads; many owners switched to higher-quality aftermarket rotors and pads to reduce recurrence. Proper lug-nut torque (even tightening) and avoiding overheating also helps. The underlying fix is upgraded rotors, as resurfacing alone tends to recur.
symptoms: Repeated need to resurface or replace rotors

records.title: Sudden Loss of Electric Power Steering Assist
records.description: The electric power steering (EPS) system on certain 2008-2009 Auras can suddenly lose assist while driving due to a faulty torque sensor or EPS motor/controller. Drivers reported the steering going heavy without warning, sometimes mid-turn, greatly increasing steering effort at low speeds. GM was criticized for being slow to recall the affected Saturn cars.
records.solution: Covered by NHTSA recall 14V153000 — dealers replaced the torque sensor assembly, the EPS motor, and/or the EPS motor controller depending on build date, at no charge. Out of warranty, repair requires replacing the EPS torque sensor or steering column motor assembly.
symptoms: Steering suddenly becomes very hard to turn
Loss of assist mid-turn or at low speed

records.title: Transmission Shift Cable Fracture (Rollaway Risk)
records.description: The plastic shift cable end fitting or its retaining tabs can wear out and fracture on automatic-transmission Auras. When this happens, the gear indicator may show 'Park' (or the wrong gear) while the transmission is actually still in Drive, Reverse, or Neutral, and the driver may be unable to shift to Park or remove the key. This created a serious vehicle rollaway hazard and was linked to multiple crashes and injuries. It is the single most-documented and safety-critical defect on the Aura, addressed by two NHTSA recalls.
records.solution: Covered by recall (NHTSA 12V460000 installed a retainer over the cable end; 14V224000 replaced the shift cable assembly and mounting bracket at no charge). Out of warranty, the fix is to replace the shift cable/shifter cable bushing or full cable assembly; some cases are resolved by replacing the small worn plastic bushing where the cable connects to the transmission lever.
symptoms: Shifter shows Park but car can still roll
Vehicle rolls when parked on an incline

records.title: 2.2L Ecotec Timing Chain Stretch and Tensioner Failure
records.description: Early 2.2L Ecotec (L61) engines have a timing chain oiling deficiency: the oiler nozzle doesn't supply enough oil at low RPM, leading to chain stretch, worn plastic guides, and a weak original tensioner that loses tension. Because the Ecotec is an interference engine, a chain that jumps time or breaks causes pistons to strike valves, often resulting in catastrophic engine damage. GM revised the tensioner/oiler for 2005, after which the problem largely disappeared.
records.solution: Replace the timing chain, tensioner, and guides with the updated parts at the first sign of rattle, before the chain jumps time. Addressing a startup or cold rattle early prevents a destroyed engine. Maintaining clean oil and regular changes reduces wear.
symptoms: Rattling or chain-slap noise, especially on cold startup
Rough running or misfire if chain has jumped time
Check engine light with camshaft/crankshaft correlation codes
Engine won't start or runs very poorly after chain skips

records.title: Ion Electric Power Steering Failure (NHTSA 14V-153)
records.description: NHTSA recall 14V-153 covers 2003-2007 Ion, 2005-2010 Cobalt, 2007-2010 Pontiac G5, 2003-2006 Pontiac Pursuit (Canada), 2008-2009 HHR for sudden loss of electric power steering assist. ~1.3 million vehicles affected. Remedy is replacement of the EPS motor or torque sensor.
records.solution: Check VIN at NHTSA recall lookup (14V-153). Repair is free under recall. If you experience sudden loss of assist, control is still possible but steering becomes very heavy — pull over safely and request roadside assistance. Do not attempt independent repair until recall status is confirmed.

records.title: Ignition Switch Can Unexpectedly Shut Off Engine (GM Defect Recall)
records.description: The ignition switch detent torque is too low, so weight on the key ring, road vibration, or a knee bump can move the switch out of the 'run' position while driving. This shuts off the engine and disables power steering, power brakes, and critically the airbags, which will not deploy in a crash if the switch is out of 'run.' This is the infamous GM ignition switch defect linked to numerous crashes and deaths, and GM established a victim compensation fund.
records.solution: Free dealer replacement of the ignition switch under NHTSA recall 14V047000. As an interim measure GM advised owners to remove all extra weight and the fob from the key ring, using only the bare ignition key. Many cars have already had the recall performed; owners can verify completion via VIN at the GM/NHTSA recall lookup.
symptoms: Engine suddenly stalls or shuts off while driving
Dash warning lights illuminate as power is lost
Loss of power steering and power brake assist after stall
Key turns off if bumped or with heavy keychain
Airbags fail to deploy in a crash

records.title: Ion Ignition Switch Recall (NHTSA 14V-047) — Same as Cobalt
records.description: NHTSA recall 14V-047 — the infamous GM ignition switch recall that triggered congressional hearings — covers 2003-2007 Ion along with 2005-2010 Cobalt, 2006-2011 HHR, 2005-2010 Pontiac G5, 2007-2010 Pontiac Solstice, 2007-2010 Saturn Sky. The switch can rotate out of "run" position due to key weight, disabling the engine and airbags during operation. Multiple deaths attributed.
records.solution: Check VIN at NHTSA recalls lookup (14V-047). Dealer replaces ignition switch and (in many cases) provides new keys with shorter shanks. Until repaired, drive with only the ignition key on the ring (no extra keys/fobs/key ring weight). Free repair under recall.

records.title: Inaccurate or Erratic Fuel Gauge (Fuel Level Sensor)
records.description: The fuel level sender inside the tank develops contaminated or worn contacts, sending erratic resistance signals to the gauge. Owners see the needle misread, drop or stick especially below a quarter tank, give false low-fuel warnings, or read empty when fuel remains. Disconnecting the battery can also throw off gauge calibration. The sender is part of the in-tank fuel pump module.
records.solution: Replace the fuel level sensor/sending unit, which generally requires dropping the fuel tank and is most economically done as part of a fuel pump module replacement. Cleaning or adjusting the sender float is a temporary fix at best. A P0463 code points to the level sensor circuit.
symptoms: Fuel gauge reads inaccurately or fluctuates
Needle sticks, drops, or reads empty with fuel in tank
False or premature low-fuel warning light
Gauge misbehaves after a battery disconnect

records.title: Interior Door Panel and Trim Rattles
records.description: The Ion's interior is prone to rattles and squeaks, most commonly from the door panels. A black plastic reinforcement strip glued along the top of the door panel can separate, and loose window glass/regulator components produce a glass-on-metal rattle over bumps, particularly with the window up or down. The glovebox door and headliner trim are also reported rattle sources. It's a cosmetic/comfort annoyance rather than a safety issue.
records.solution: Remove the affected door panel and re-secure or re-glue the loose plastic reinforcement, add foam/felt to contact points, and check the window regulator and glass run channels. Tightening or padding the glovebox and trim clips resolves the other rattles. Largely a DIY fix.
symptoms: Rattling or buzzing from door panels over bumps
Glass-on-metal rattle with the window up or down
Glovebox door and headliner trim rattle
Loose or separated trim along the top of the door panel

citations.title: Interior Door Trim Rattle (SaturnFans.com Forums)

records.title: Key Stuck in Ignition / Worn Lock Cylinder
records.description: Separate from the safety recall, Ion owners frequently report the key sticking in the ignition or refusing to turn fully off, often getting trapped in the ACC position. This stems from a worn ignition lock cylinder, worn key teeth, or a faulty Brake-Transmission Shift Interlock (BTSI) solenoid that should release the lock when the car is in Park. It can leave the key trapped and accessory power on, risking a dead battery.
records.solution: Replace the ignition lock cylinder and/or worn key; if the interlock is the cause, replace the BTSI solenoid/switch. As a temporary workaround, ensure the shifter is fully in Park and gently jiggle the key. A locksmith or dealer can re-key a new cylinder to the existing key.
symptoms: Key will not come out of the ignition
Key gets stuck in the ACC (accessory) position
Engine won't shut off / accessory power stays on
Key hard to insert, turn, or remove

records.title: Sudden Loss of Electric Power Steering Assist
records.description: The electric power steering (EPS) motor can suddenly lose assist at any time while driving, often mid-turn or at low speed, due to brush debris and oily contamination disrupting the EPS motor. Steering remains mechanically connected but requires much greater effort, especially during parking and low-speed maneuvers, raising crash risk. NHTSA received over 800 Ion complaints and ran a multi-year investigation (PE10-018); the Ion was excluded from GM's 2010 recall and not recalled until 2014.
records.solution: Free replacement of the electric power steering motor under NHTSA recall 14V153000 (began July 2014). 2004-2007 Ions are covered by GM bulletin 14115; 2003 Ions received EPS motor replacement coverage for the life of the vehicle under bulletin 14119. Outside the recall, the fix is the same EPS motor/column assembly replacement.
symptoms: Steering wheel suddenly becomes very hard to turn
Power steering warning light or message
Loss of assist occurs intermittently, sometimes mid-turn
Extra effort needed when parking or at low speed

records.title: VTi CVT Transmission Failure
records.description: The Ion's optional VTi continuously variable transmission (GM's first high-volume CVT) is notoriously unreliable. The steel push-belt and related internals wear or fail, causing slipping, harsh or no engagement, and eventually complete loss of drive. GM halted VTi production in January 2004 due to durability problems and a class-action lawsuit covering roughly 90,000 Ion and Vue vehicles was settled.
records.solution: Failed VTi units typically require full transmission replacement or rebuild; some intermittent no-drive cases were addressed by replacing the case cover assembly, torque converter, and oil cooler lines. The class-action settlement extended coverage to 5 years/75,000 miles from new. Many owners ultimately swap to the conventional automatic or buy a known-good unit.
symptoms: Transmission slipping or flaring under acceleration
Delayed or no engagement into drive or reverse
Loss of forward motion / car won't move

records.title: Outlook Power Steering Assist Loss — GM Special Coverage 14329
records.description: GM Special Coverage Adjustment 14329 extends warranty to 10 years / 150,000 miles for power-steering pump wear on 2007-2010 Saturn Outlook, 2007-2011 GMC Acadia, 2008-2011 Buick Enclave, 2009-2011 Chevrolet Traverse. The pump wears internally, causing intermittent drop in hydraulic pressure and loss of steering assist — heavy steering at low speed, particularly when the engine is hot. This is a special coverage program, NOT a recall — owners must initiate the claim. (Note: a fire-risk recall on this PS hose does NOT exist; only the PS-assist-loss special coverage.)
records.solution: Confirm Special Coverage 14329 eligibility at any GM dealer with your VIN. If still within 10 years and 150,000 miles, remedy is free: dealer flushes power-steering system, replaces the PS pump, installs a new steering-gear valve housing. If out of the coverage window, expect $700-$1,400 for the same job at an independent.

records.title: DIS Ignition Module / Coil Pack Failure Causing Cylinder Misfires
records.description: The Saturn S-Series uses a Distributorless Ignition System (DIS) with a waste-spark coil pack mounted on top of the engine. The coils and the Ignition Control Module (ICM) fail with age, throwing P0300-series misfire codes (commonly P0301 or P0302). A subtle but documented contributor is poor grounding: the ICM grounds to the transmission bellhousing via a stud, and corrosion on this ground path causes intermittent misfires that are easily misdiagnosed as coil failure. The waste-spark design uses the #4 plug firing on the compression stroke to fake a cam signal, so if the #4 coil weakens, the DIS may also lose its cam-position reference, causing cascading driveability issues.
records.solution: Diagnose by swapping the suspect coil with a known-good cylinder coil — if the misfire follows the coil, replace it. Before condemning the coil pack, inspect and clean the ICM-to-transmission ground stud: remove the bolt, wire-brush the contact surface on the transmission case down to bare metal, apply dielectric grease, and reinstall. Also clean and grease the ICM connectors. If grounds and coil swap don't fix it, replace the full coil pack assembly (~$80-150). Always replace the spark plugs and plug wires at the same time — the OE Champion plugs are specified for this engine; aftermarket platinum/iridium can cause its own misfires on the waste-spark system. Torque coil bolts carefully; the aluminum threads strip easily.
symptoms: Misfire DTC P0301, P0302, P0303, or P0304
Rough idle or shaking at idle
Check Engine Light (often flashing under load)

records.title: EGR Valve Clogging Causing P0401/P0404/P1404 Codes
records.description: Beginning with OBD-II in 1996, the Saturn S-Series 1.9L EGR system is highly susceptible to carbon clogging. The narrow gap between the EGR pintle and its passage is easily fouled by exhaust carbon, especially on engines that burn oil (a chronic issue on this engine — see the oil consumption issue). The most common codes are P0401 (insufficient EGR flow), P0404 (EGR control circuit range/performance), and the Saturn-specific P1404 (EGR closed position). Replacing the valve alone rarely fixes the problem because the EGR passages in the cylinder head and intake manifold are also clogged. The condition worsens markedly once oil consumption begins.
records.solution: Remove the EGR valve and clean it: fill the valve body with carb cleaner, soak for 15 minutes, drain, and repeat 5-10 times. Use a T-handle Torx driver to manually work the pintle up and down to break free carbon deposits. Critically, also clean the EGR passages in the intake manifold and the supply tube/passage in the cylinder head — these are usually more clogged than the valve itself. A wire brush, pipe cleaners, and aerosol carb cleaner work well. If oil consumption is significant, expect the EGR to re-clog within 10,000-20,000 miles. Address oil consumption first for a lasting fix. Replacement EGR valves are inexpensive (~$50-80) but useless if the passages are not cleaned.
symptoms: Check Engine Light with code P0401, P0404, or P1404
Stalling when coming to a stop

records.title: Intake Manifold Gasket Coolant Leak at Cylinder #4 (DOHC 1.9L)
records.description: The 1.9L DOHC engine in the Saturn S-Series suffers from an intake manifold gasket failure where the OE one-piece gasket experiences compression set in the coolant passage between the manifold and the cylinder head, specifically at cylinder #4. Coolant leaks externally during cold-engine operation, sometimes evaporating before pooling on the ground, leading to mysterious coolant loss. A Saturn TSB documents the issue and the redesigned fix: a two-piece gasket consisting of a shorter orange intake manifold seal plus a separate black coolant seal made of a different elastomer. Most failures appear after 60,000 miles. The plastic intake manifold itself is also prone to broken coolant nipples.
records.solution: Replace the OE one-piece intake manifold gasket with Saturn's revised two-piece design (orange intake gasket + separate black coolant seal). Removal of the intake manifold also gives access to inspect and replace the brittle plastic coolant nipples that protrude from the manifold — these commonly snap off during service. Use new manifold bolts torqued to spec in the proper sequence. Total job is about 2-3 hours of labor. Always pressure-test the cooling system after the repair to verify the seal. While the intake is off, this is also a good time to clean the EGR passages, which are typically clogged on these engines.
symptoms: Coolant loss with no obvious puddle
Sweet coolant smell after cold start
Visible coolant residue near cylinder #4 intake port
Steam from engine bay during warm-up
Low coolant warning despite recent top-off

records.title: S-Series 1.9L DOHC Oil Consumption (Coked Piston Rings)
records.description: The 1.9L DOHC engine in SL2 / SC2 / SW2 develops excessive oil consumption (often 1 qt per 1,000 miles or worse) by 80,000-150,000 miles. Root cause is coked oil-control rings — common to the engine's open-deck design and high tolerance for low-quality oil over its long life. Owners are sometimes startled to find the engine 2+ quarts low between changes.
records.solution: Ring-cleaning treatments (BG EPR, Sea Foam soak) cycled through oil changes can sometimes free coked rings. If consumption is >1 qt/1,000 miles, ring/piston replacement (~$1,500-$2,500) is the durable fix. Many owners simply top off and run the car until something else fails — these engines often pass 250,000 miles even with consumption.

records.title: S-Series 1.9L Valve Cover & Front Crank Seal Leaks
records.description: The 1.9L SOHC (SL/SC1) and DOHC (SL2/SC2) engines in 1991-2002 S-Series sedans (SL), coupes (SC), and wagons (SW) develop persistent oil leaks at the valve cover gasket and front crank seal by 80,000-120,000 miles. The DOHC valve cover gasket is a $20 part but the cover bolt holes strip easily. The front crank seal often leaks onto the timing chain area and drips onto the exhaust manifold causing smell.
records.solution: Valve cover gasket replacement DIY (~$30 part); use a torque wrench to spec (89 in-lbs) to avoid stripping. Front crank seal requires harmonic balancer removal — $200-$400 at independent. Replace the cam seals at the same time on DOHC. If valve cover bolt holes are stripped, time-serts ($60-$100) save the head.
symptoms: oil dripping from front of engine

records.title: SC Coupe Third (Suicide) Door Hinge Sag & Latch Wear
records.description: 1999-2002 Saturn SC 3-door coupes have a small rear-hinged "suicide" door on the driver side for rear-seat access. The door is heavy for its hinges and develops sag, leading to alignment issues, weatherstrip wear, and difficult close. The latch mechanism is also prone to wear with regular use.
records.solution: Hinge bushings replacement (~$30 parts, 1 hour labor). Door realignment ($60-$120 shop) often needed simultaneously. Latch wear requires latch assembly replacement (~$100-$200 part) or attempt cleaning and re-lubricating internal pawl. If the steel door pin is worn, replace the pin and bushing kit before more hinge damage occurs.

records.title: Sky Ignition Switch Recall (NHTSA 14V-047 — Same as Ion)
records.description: NHTSA recall 14V-047 includes 2007-2010 Saturn Sky (along with Ion, Cobalt, HHR, G5, Solstice). The ignition switch can rotate out of "run" position due to key weight, disabling engine, power steering, brake boost, and airbags during operation.
records.solution: Check VIN at NHTSA recall lookup (14V-047). Free dealer ignition switch replacement under recall. Until repaired, drive with only the ignition key on the ring — no extra weight from fobs or key rings.

records.title: Sky Trunk Leak with Top Down (Kappa Platform)
records.description: 2007-2010 Saturn Sky (and Pontiac Solstice / Opel GT — all Kappa platform) has the trunk lid integrate with the soft top stowage. With the top down, the trunk seal is exposed; rain leaks past the seal into the trunk well. Tiny trunk space (only 3.8 cu ft with top stowed) means water pools at the spare-tire well and rusts the floor panel.
records.solution: Replace trunk seal if cracked ($60-$120 part); inspect annually. Use 3M weatherstrip adhesive to reseal. Always check spare-tire well after heavy rain. Confirm the top stowage drainage gutters are clear.
symptoms: standing water in spare tire well

records.title: 3.6L High Feature V6 (LY7) Timing Chain Stretch
records.description: The 3.6L 'High Feature' V6 used in the redesigned 2008-2010 Vue (and shared with Aura/Outlook/Acadia/CTS) is prone to timing chain stretch, often aggravated by extended oil-change intervals. As the chains and plastic guides wear, cam/crank timing drifts out of correlation, triggering the check-engine light, rough running, and a rattle on cold start. GM issued Information Bulletin 12-06-01-009F covering timing chain kit and guide replacement for DTCs P0008/P0009/P0016/P0017/P0018/P0019.
records.solution: Verify oil level and condition first; severely stretched chains require replacing the timing chains, tensioners, and guides as a complete set (often all three chains on this engine). Owners can reduce risk by using the correct dexos1-spec oil and changing it at conservative (e.g., ~5,000-mile) intervals rather than relying on the oil-life monitor's longer recommendations.
symptoms: Rattle or rattling on cold start

Common Diagnostic Trouble Codes - GM LY7 3.6L V6 | Highline Car Care

records.title: Vue 3.5L Honda V6 Timing Belt Service Interval
records.description: 2004-2007 Saturn Vue V6 used the Honda 3.5L J35 V6 (sourced from Honda) — same engine as the Honda Pilot/Odyssey/MDX. It uses a timing belt with a recommended replacement interval of 100,000 miles (or 7 years). Interference engine: failure to replace the belt risks catastrophic valve damage. Water pump should be replaced at the same time.
records.solution: Full timing belt + water pump + tensioner + idler service kit ($600-$1,000 at independent). Use OEM Honda or quality aftermarket Gates/Aisin parts. Do NOT exceed the interval — this is an interference design. Some owners replaced at 90,000 miles for extra margin.

records.title: Automatic Transmission Park Pawl Casting Defect Recall (08V200)
records.description: Certain 2008 Vue vehicles were recalled (NHTSA campaign 08V200000) for a casting defect in the automatic transmission case that can compromise the park pawl, eliminating the transmission's ability to be secured in Park. A vehicle left in Park can roll away, creating a crash hazard. This is a distinct issue from the earlier VTi CVT failures.
records.solution: Under the recall, dealers replace the affected transmission at no charge to the owner. Owners of 2008 Vues should check their VIN against open recalls and, as a precaution, always set the parking brake when parking until the remedy is confirmed complete.
symptoms: Transmission does not hold in Park position

records.title: Front Subframe / Lateral Link Corrosion in Salt-Belt Regions
records.description: Owners in northern, road-salt states report premature corrosion of the front subframe/cradle and rear lateral (suspension) links on early Vues, with cases of the subframe rusting through and causing unstable steering. GM acknowledged related rear lateral-link issues, and rear wheel/lateral link concerns were addressed under earlier recall activity. Severe corrosion can make the vehicle unsafe to drive and is expensive to repair on an older vehicle.
records.solution: Have the subframe, control arms, and rear lateral links inspected for structural rust, especially before purchase in salt-belt areas; corroded structural members must be replaced. Regular undercarriage washing and rust-inhibitor treatment can slow further corrosion on otherwise sound vehicles.

records.title: Ignition Key Can Be Removed When Not in 'Off' — Rollaway Recall (14V490)
records.description: On affected 2002-2004 Vue vehicles, the ignition lock cylinder can wear such that the key may be removed when the ignition is not in the 'Off' position. If the key is pulled with an automatic transmission not in Park (or a manual without the parking brake set), the vehicle can roll away unexpectedly. GM recalled roughly 202,000 Vues (NHTSA campaign 14V490000) and acknowledged crashes and at least one injury tied to the defect.
records.solution: Under the recall, dealers inspect whether the key can be removed when the ignition is not in Off; if so, they replace the ignition lock cylinder and re-key it to the existing keys at no charge. Owners can verify open recalls by VIN on the NHTSA website and have the remedy performed free at any GM dealer.
symptoms: Key can be pulled out when ignition is in Run or Accessory
Vehicle rolls away after key removal
Ignition cylinder feels worn or loose

records.title: Power Steering Line Nut Loosening — Leak and Fire Recall (08V470)
records.description: On 2008-2009 Vue models, the nut securing the power steering line to the power steering pump can loosen, allowing high-pressure power steering fluid to leak. The fluid can contact hot exhaust components and potentially cause an engine-compartment fire. GM recalled 42,408 vehicles under NHTSA campaign 08V470000. Many owners separately reported sudden loss of power steering assist with no warning, and some VINs were not included in the recall population.
records.solution: Under the recall, dealers inspect the power steering line nut; if no leak is present they tighten it, and if a leak is found they tighten the nut and top off/verify the fluid. Owners experiencing ongoing leaks or loss of assist outside the recall should have the pump, lines, and rack-and-pinion seals inspected for the leak source.
symptoms: Low or empty power steering reservoir
Sudden loss of power steering assist

records.title: V6 Valve Cover Gasket Oil Leak Soaking Coil Boots → Misfires
records.description: On the 3.0L and 3.5L V6 Vue models, the valve cover gaskets become brittle and leak oil down into the spark plug tubes. The oil soaks the coil-on-plug boots, causing the rubber to swell and degrade so spark grounds out, producing misfires and rough running. Oil also drips onto the exhaust manifold, creating a burning-oil smell.
records.solution: Replace the leaking valve cover gaskets and clean oil from the spark plug tubes, then replace the oil-soaked coil boots (and plugs if fouled). Replacing only the boots without fixing the valve cover gasket leak leads to repeat failure, so address the gasket as the root cause.

records.title: VTi (VT25-E) Continuously Variable Transmission Failure
records.description: The 4-cylinder Vue's VTi CVT was GM's first high-volume CVT and proved badly unreliable, with the steel push-belt and related components wearing out prematurely. Owners experienced slipping, shuddering, jerky/erratic shifting, loud whining on acceleration, and sudden power loss, with many units failing entirely between 50,000 and 100,000 miles. GM halted VTi production in January 2004 and later settled a class-action lawsuit covering more than 90,000 Saturn Vue and Ion vehicles. This is the single most-reported Vue problem on owner-complaint databases.
records.solution: There was no durable repair; failed units were replaced with rebuilt/replacement transmissions costing roughly $3,500-$5,000. GM extended the powertrain warranty on VTi units to 5 years/75,000 miles and provided reimbursement under the class-action settlement. Many owners with later failures opted to replace the vehicle rather than the transmission given its high cost relative to resale value.

records.title: Vue VTi CVT Catastrophic Failure (2002-2005)
records.description: Early Saturn Vue (2002-2005) was offered with the GM VT25 (VTi) continuously-variable transmission paired with the 2.2L Ecotec. The CVT was infamously unreliable — failure rates so high that GM extended warranty to 5 years/75,000 miles, and many independents won't touch them. Symptoms: belt slip noise, surge under acceleration, eventual no-drive.
records.solution: If still under the extended warranty, get it documented. If out of warranty, the practical options are: (1) used VTi CVT swap (~$1,200-$2,500 with risky reliability), (2) used 5-speed manual conversion ($1,500-$3,000 with parts hunt), or (3) part out / sell the vehicle. Aamco / GM dealers historically offered swap-with-Aisin-5-speed conversions but parts are hard to source.
